prompt.context: A leading automobile manufacturer has had a sharp decline in retail sales in the first quarter of 2017. They have approached you to identify the root causes of the problem and to fix them.
prompt.question: What are the root causes of the sharp decline in retail sales in Q1 2017, and how would you fix them?

clarifying_info.q: Is the scope limited to a specific geography?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, the scope of the problem is limited to sales in the US.

clarifying_info.q: How is 'sale' defined in this context?
clarifying_info.a: Manufacturer's sale (primary sale) is defined as the sale to the dealership. Final sale (retail) is the sale to the end customer by the dealership.

exhibits.title: Sales Figures 2016 - US (All models - # of cars)
exhibits.shows: Monthly primary sale (manufacturer to dealership) and retail sale (dealership to end customer) figures for each month of 2016, organized by quarter.

exhibits.title: US Sales Analysis Report 2016
exhibits.shows: Monthly and quarterly funnel data showing Enquiries, Test Drives, Bookings, and Retail Sales for all four quarters of 2016.

framework: Define scope: US retail sales decline in Q1 2017
Distinguish primary sales (manufacturer to dealer) vs. retail sales (dealer to customer)
Check for inventory build-up: compare primary vs. retail sales to detect excess stock at dealerships
Analyze the sales funnel: Enquiries → Test Drives → Bookings → Retail Sales to find conversion breakdowns
Identify root cause of funnel weakness (regional issues, staffing/turnover, product mix, incentives)
Recommend targeted interventions to clear excess inventory and restore conversion rates

questions.prompt: Look at Exhibit 1. What do you observe about Q4 2016 primary vs. retail sales, and what does that imply for Q1 2017?
questions.guidance: Candidate should notice that in Q4 2016 primary sales consistently exceeded retail sales each month, creating dealer inventory build-up. They should quantify the excess stock as a percentage of primary sales and conclude that this inventory overhang suppressed manufacturer primary sales in Q1 2017.

math.setup: For each month in Q4, compute stock build-up = Primary Sale − Retail Sale. Sum Q4 stock build-up, then divide by total Q4 primary sales.
steps: Excess inventory as % of Q4 primary sales: 4,939 / 43,116 ≈ 11–13%
math.answer: Approximately 13% of Q4 primary sales became excess inventory at dealerships, explaining why dealers did not need to order as many cars from the manufacturer in Q1 2017.

questions.prompt: Given Exhibit 2 (the sales funnel), where in the funnel does performance weaken in Q4 2016?
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate conversion ratios at each stage across all four quarters and compare Q4 to earlier quarters. The key finding is that Q4 Test Drive to Bookings conversion drops sharply (~17%) versus ~24–25% in Q1–Q3. Enquiries-to-Test-Drive is stable at ~10% all year. Bookings-to-Retail is broadly consistent (~88–93%). This pinpoints the Test Drive to Booking step as the Q4 weakness.

math.setup: For each quarter, calculate: (1) Enquiries to Test Drives = TD / Enquiries; (2) Test Drives to Bookings = Bookings / TD; (3) Bookings to Retail = Retail / Bookings.
math.answer: Q4 Test Drive to Booking conversion fell to ~17%, down from ~23–25% in previous quarters. Enquiries-to-Test-Drive and Bookings-to-Retail ratios held steady, isolating the drop-off at the Test Drive → Booking stage.

brainstorming.prompt: Why might the Test Drive to Booking conversion rate have dropped sharply in Q4? What could be causing this, and how could it be fixed?

categories.name: Sales force issues
ideas: Unexpected turnover among sales staff in Q4 (holiday season departures, year-end bonuses driving moves)
Undertrained or new sales staff unable to close after test drives
Misaligned or insufficient Q4 sales incentives
Low morale or burnout heading into year-end

categories.name: Product / inventory mix issues
ideas: Overstocked models that customers do not want after the test drive
New model year arriving, making current inventory feel stale
Pricing or feature mismatch between what customers enquire about and what is actually available on the lot

categories.name: External / seasonal factors
ideas: Holiday-season budget constraints leading customers to delay purchase decisions
Higher competition from other brands running year-end promotions
Tighter credit availability in Q4 affecting financing approvals

categories.name: Regional performance
ideas: One or more specific regions severely underperforming on conversion (pulling down the national average)
Dealership-level issues such as poor customer experience or specific management problems

categories.name: Solutions / interventions
ideas: Realign sales incentives to reward test-drive-to-booking conversion, not just footfall
Offer targeted discounts or financing deals on overstocked models to close deals at point of test drive
Investigate and address regional outliers with targeted management action
Conduct exit surveys with customers who test-drove but did not book to understand objections
Ensure adequate and well-trained staffing through Q4 with retention bonuses

recommendation: In Q4 2016 primary sales outpaced retail sales, building roughly 4,939 units (~13% of Q4 primary volume) of excess dealer inventory, which suppressed manufacturer orders in Q1 2017.

The root cause of the retail shortfall is a sharp drop in Test Drive to Booking conversion (from ~24% in Q1–Q3 to ~17% in Q4), not a drop in customer interest (enquiries and test drives were at their highest in Q4).
risks: Inventory overhang may persist into Q2 2017 if conversion is not restored quickly, further delaying primary sales recovery.
If the TD-to-booking drop reflects a structural issue (product competitiveness, pricing), short-term incentives will not be sufficient.
Regional or dealer-level issues may require bespoke solutions and take longer to resolve.
next_steps: Obtain data to understand why TD-to-booking conversion dropped — conduct exit interviews, analyze by region and by dealership.
Check whether the Q4 conversion weakness persists into Q1 2017.
Design targeted interventions: revised incentive structures, financing promotions on overstocked models, and staffing/training reviews.
Request additional data on competitor activity in Q4 and credit/financing approval rates to rule out external causes.
